applies_when: Vivado 2026.1 cannot identify event control as a single clock plus valid asynchronous control during synth_design.
guidance: First read the diagnostic order in the same group: 8-7213 indicates a mismatch between condition polarity and event edge, and a subsequent 8-462 may be a cascading result; 8-91 indicates that multiple edges may be interpreted as clocks.
Before making changes, confirm the clock, reset synchronicity, active level, and priority required by the specification.
hard_negatives: posedge clk with negedge rst_n and a condition using !rst_n IS a common legal asynchronous active-low reset template.
MUST NOT change synchronous reset to asynchronous reset solely to eliminate the error.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN the process inherently describes combinational logic, or when the error originates from general syntax and type checking in xvlog/xelab.

applies_when: The specification confirms the object is sequential state, and event control or reset conditions cause Synth 8-462, 8-7213, or 8-91.
guidance: Record the unique clock edge, reset synchronicity, reset active level, reset value, and priority separately.
For asynchronous reset, add only the edge consistent with the active level in the event control; for synchronous reset, evaluate only within the clock edge.
Keep all normal state updates under the same clock ownership; DO NOT use a second clock edge to replace enable.
hard_negatives: The posedge of two functional clocks MUST NOT be disguised as one clock plus reset by adjusting if order.
Deleting the reset edge may silently change an asynchronous reset to a synchronous reset.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN the object should be combinational logic, or when the specification does not allow asynchronous reset, asynchronous set, or a second clock.

applies_when: Source code uses bit indexing, array indexing, part-select, or generate loop indices on packed vectors or unpacked arrays.
guidance: Record packed/unpacked status, declared left/right endpoints, legal index sets, and element width for each dimension; DO NOT guess shape based on signal names.
For part-select, simultaneously verify that endpoints are within range, direction matches the declaration, and result width is correct.
Generate loop bounds MUST ensure that all dimension indices obtained from each expansion are legal.
hard_negatives: Expanding object declarations and shortening loop upper bounds both eliminate out-of-bounds errors, but only the one conforming to the interface and specification IS the correct fix.
Range direction errors and numerical out-of-bounds errors ARE different problems; DO NOT skip width checks by merely swapping endpoints.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN the object declaration is invisible, or when the current failure involves only arithmetic result bit width without selection operations.
cards.projection_text:
[Knowledge Card semantic-selection-shape@1.1.0-en.candidate.1] Expand object dimensions, legal indices, and bit order before selection
applies_when: Source code uses bit indexing, array indexing, part-select, or generate loop indices on packed vectors or unpacked arrays.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN the object declaration is invisible, or when the current failure involves only arithmetic result bit width without selection operations.
guidance: Record packed/unpacked status, declared left/right endpoints, legal index sets, and element width for each dimension; DO NOT guess shape based on signal names.; For part-select, simultaneously verify that endpoints are within range, direction matches the declaration, and result width is correct.; Generate loop bounds MUST ensure that all dimension indices obtained from each expansion are legal.
verification: Check at least the minimum index, maximum index, and adjacent boundaries for each dimension, and let xvlog/xelab re-expand the generate structure.
hard_negatives: Expanding object declarations and shortening loop upper bounds both eliminate out-of-bounds errors, but only the one conforming to the interface and specification IS the correct fix.; Range direction errors and numerical out-of-bounds errors ARE different problems; DO NOT skip width checks by merely swapping endpoints.
cards.title: Expand object dimensions, legal indices, and bit order before selection
verification: Check at least the minimum index, maximum index, and adjacent boundaries for each dimension, and let xvlog/xelab re-expand the generate structure.

applies_when: Declaration shape and selection location are visible, and tool evidence points to index out-of-bounds, generate bounds, or part-select direction.
guidance: First use semantic-selection-shape to write out the legal index set, then decide whether to fix the declaration, loop bounds, or selection endpoints.
Maintain interface port names, directions, and specification widths; DO NOT mechanically expand arrays solely to pass tools.
When modifying part-select, simultaneously maintain direction, bit order, and target width.
hard_negatives: Changing the for loop upper bound from 4 to 3 and changing the array size from 3 to 4 may both compile, but they have different functional meanings.
Swapping [msb:lsb] endpoints may change bit order.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN the object width required by the interface or specification is not yet determined, or when the error originates from undeclared identifiers.

verification: Re-run xvlog/xelab or synthesis, and perform functional checks for minimum, maximum, and adjacent out-of-bounds values.

applies_when: VRFC 10-2063 indicates the module cannot be found when processing an instance, or 10-3640 indicates a name in the module formal port list is not defined.
guidance: For 10-2063, first check if the source file is included in compilation, the module declaration name, and the instance type name; for 10-3640, check the module's own port list and body declaration.
DO NOT confuse module not found with instance connection port not found as the same error.
hard_negatives: "cannot find port on this module" belongs to instance connection checking and IS NOT equivalent to module not found.
MUST NOT eliminate resolution errors by deleting instances or arbitrarily changing the problem interface.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN the module and formal ports exist, but the instance naming connection, direction, bit width, or parameters do not match.

[Knowledge Card diag-design-unit-resolution@1.1.0-en.candidate.1] VRFC 10-2063 and 10-3640 point to module resolution and formal port definition respectively
applies_when: VRFC 10-2063 indicates the module cannot be found when processing an instance, or 10-3640 indicates a name in the module formal port list is not defined.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN the module and formal ports exist, but the instance naming connection, direction, bit width, or parameters do not match.
guidance: For 10-2063, first check if the source file is included in compilation, the module declaration name, and the instance type name; for 10-3640, check the module's own port list and body declaration.; DO NOT confuse module not found with instance connection port not found as the same error.
verification: First run xvlog to compile all design units, then use xelab to elaborate the target top level.
hard_negatives: "cannot find port on this module" belongs to instance connection checking and IS NOT equivalent to module not found.; MUST NOT eliminate resolution errors by deleting instances or arbitrarily changing the problem interface.
cards.title: VRFC 10-2063 and 10-3640 point to module resolution and formal port definition respectively
verification: First run xvlog to compile all design units, then use xelab to elaborate the target top level.

applies_when: Tool evidence indicates that module declarations, compile inputs, or formal port lists cannot be resolved.
guidance: Verify the target top-level name, whether source files are compiled, each module declaration name, instance type name, and formal port set in sequence.
Interface names MUST follow the public problem statement; prioritize fixing spelling, omissions, and compile inputs; DO NOT create empty shell modules to mask missing implementations.
Handle instance connections after compilation is complete; DO NOT guess port fixes while modules are not yet resolved.
hard_negatives: The existence of a file with the same name DOES NOT mean it declares the correct module.
Creating non-functional placeholder modules may allow elaboration to pass, but WILL cause subsequent functional failures.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN design units have been resolved successfully, and only instance connection bit width, parameter values, or functional errors exist.

applies_when: The same identifier appears undeclared, used before explicit declaration, duplicated in the same scope, or suspected of scope shadowing.
guidance: Build a declaration table for each scope, recording name, type, width, declaration location, and first use location.

For completely undeclared identifiers, restore the real object from the specification; for use-before-declaration, move the unique declaration before the first use; for same-scope duplicates, compare the intent of both locations and keep one.
DO NOT rely on implicit nets; SystemVerilog design code SHOULD prefer explicit declarations and maintain original driving style and width.
hard_negatives: ANSI style port duplicate declarations SHOULD use port rules and MUST NOT apply general local declaration fixes.
Legal block-local variables or generate block name reuse MUST NOT be deleted merely because they share the same name.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN the error is explicitly an ANSI port re-declared in the module body, or when the name is merely reused in different legal nested scopes.
cards.projection_text:
[Knowledge Card semantic-declaration-lifecycle@1.1.0-en.candidate.1] Classify declaration issues by scope, first use, and declaration count
applies_when: The same identifier appears undeclared, used before explicit declaration, duplicated in the same scope, or suspected of scope shadowing.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN the error is explicitly an ANSI port re-declared in the module body, or when the name is merely reused in different legal nested scopes.
guidance: Build a declaration table for each scope, recording name, type, width, declaration location, and first use location.; For completely undeclared identifiers, restore the real object from the specification; for use-before-declaration, move the unique declaration before the first use; for same-scope duplicates, compare the intent of both locations and keep one.; DO NOT rely on implicit nets; SystemVerilog design code SHOULD prefer explicit declarations and maintain original driving style and width.
verification: Re-run xvlog to confirm implicit and duplicate declaration diagnostics disappear, then check that all references still bind to the expected object in the intended scope.
hard_negatives: ANSI style port duplicate declarations SHOULD use port rules and MUST NOT apply general local declaration fixes.; Legal block-local variables or generate block name reuse MUST NOT be deleted merely because they share the same name.
cards.title: Classify declaration issues by scope, first use, and declaration count
verification: Re-run xvlog to confirm implicit and duplicate declaration diagnostics disappear, then check that all references still bind to the expected object in the intended scope.

applies_when: xvlog reports that an object has already been implicitly declared, or a second explicit declaration exists in the same scope.
guidance: First identify all declarations and references, then retain one explicit declaration with correct type and width, placing it before the first use.

Before merging duplicate declarations, compare type, signedness, packed/unpacked dimensions, and initialization item by item; if conflicts exist, refer to the interface or functional specification for a decision, and DO NOT arbitrarily select one location.
When fixing reference order, DO NOT create a new wire with the same name to mask the original signal, and DO NOT batch rename unrelated objects.
hard_negatives: Deleting the earlier declaration may cause the first use to become an implicit net again.
Uniformly replacing all duplicate names will break legal nested scopes and hierarchical references.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN the diagnostic is an ANSI port redeclaration, a completely undeclared identifier, an enum member revalue, or legal nested scope shadowing.

applies_when: xvlog reports that an object has already been implicitly declared, or a second explicit declaration exists in the same scope.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN the diagnostic is an ANSI port redeclaration, a completely undeclared identifier, an enum member revalue, or legal nested scope shadowing.

verification: Run xvlog to confirm the corresponding diagnostic disappears; search the same scope to ensure only one declaration remains, and check that procedurally driven objects still use allowed variable types.
hard_negatives: Deleting the earlier declaration may cause the first use to become an implicit net again.; Uniformly replacing all duplicate names will break legal nested scopes and hierarchical references.
cards.title: Repair implicit declaration order and same-scope duplicates with a single explicit declaration

applies_when: The expression is used for declaration bit width or range, parameterized arrays, generate conditions, or generate loop bounds.
guidance: Determine if the expression depends only on parameter, localparam, constant functions, literals, or genvar before elaboration.
Ordinary integer, logic, input ports, and procedural assignment results are runtime objects; DO NOT treat them as declaration range constants just because their values appear fixed.
Parameter values should retain a configurable contract; change to localparam only when the specification requires a fixed internal module value.
hard_negatives: An integer variable in a procedural for loop can legally control runtime iteration but DOES NOT directly replace the elaboration index of a generate.
Dynamic bit selection can use runtime indices, but this DOES NOT mean declaration width can also use runtime signals.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN the expression is only computed at runtime in an always block, or it is merely a dynamic bit selection on an already declared vector.
cards.projection_text:
[Knowledge Card semantic-elaboration-constant@1.1.0-en.candidate.1] Bit width, range, and generate conditions must be evaluable at elaboration
applies_when: The expression is used for declaration bit width or range, parameterized arrays, generate conditions, or generate loop bounds.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN the expression is only computed at runtime in an always block, or it is merely a dynamic bit selection on an already declared vector.

cards.title: Bit width, range, and generate conditions must be evaluable at elaboration
verification: Run xvlog/xelab with default parameters and at least one legal override value, checking declaration ranges and generated instance counts.

applies_when: A generate for loop is missing a genvar, or the declared type of the loop index is inconsistent with the stage in which the loop resides.
guidance: Use an independent genvar for generate for loops, ensuring the initial value, termination condition, and step are evaluable at elaboration.
Use integer or appropriate procedural variables for procedural for loops; DO NOT move runtime behavior into generate just to eliminate diagnostics.
After fixing the index type, continue to verify array bounds and connections for each expanded instance.
hard_negatives: Changing a procedural loop variable to genvar will change the execution stage and hardware structure.
Adding only a genvar without checking the loop upper bound may still produce out-of-bounds instances during expansion.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN the loop is located in a procedural block such as always/initial and requires runtime iteration, or the actual issue is an out-of-bounds array index after generation.

applies_when: A generate for loop is missing a genvar, or the declared type of the loop index is inconsistent with the stage in which the loop resides.

verification: Run xvlog first, then use xelab to check the number of expanded instances, hierarchical names, and selection bounds for each iteration.

applies_when: Explicit or implicit values of typedef enum members are duplicated, or candidate values may exceed the width and signed range of the enum base type.
guidance: List the expanded numerical value of each enum member, checking uniqueness, base type bit width, and signedness.
Width should be determined by required state encoding and specification; DO NOT blindly expand the state register just to accommodate one incorrect constant.
After modifying the encoding, synchronously verify case branches, state reset values, comparison expressions, and externally visible encoding contracts.
hard_negatives: Different localparams having the same numerical value is legally allowed in the language; DO NOT apply enum uniqueness rules to them.
Expanding the enum base type may accommodate values but may change interface width and the illegal state space.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN duplicate constants do not belong to the same enum, or the error is merely truncation in ordinary vector assignment.

applies_when: Module instances, continuous assignments, or other module items appear outside any module declaration, or module/endmodule pairing causes content to fall into compilation scope.
guidance: First mark the boundaries from each module to endmodule, then confirm the instance belongs to the expected parent module or a legal generate block.
Prioritize fixing missing, extra, or misplaced module/endmodule; DO NOT mask boundary errors by deleting instances.
After restoring boundaries, check submodule resolution and port connections to avoid treating subsequent diagnostics as the current root cause.
hard_negatives: Failing to find a submodule inside a module is a design unit resolution issue, NOT a compilation scope error.
Legal packages, interfaces, or compilation directives MUST NOT be mechanically wrapped into a module just because they are outside a module.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN the instance is already inside a module, but the instantiated design unit is not compiled or the module name does not exist.
cards.projection_text:
[Knowledge Card semantic-module-compilation-scope@1.1.0-en.candidate.1] Module instances must be located in a legal scope within a design unit
applies_when: Module instances, continuous assignments, or other module items appear outside any module declaration, or module/endmodule pairing causes content to fall into compilation scope.

verification: Run xvlog to check that compilation scope diagnostics disappear, then use xelab to expand the target top level and confirm the instance is in the expected hierarchy.
hard_negatives: Failing to find a submodule inside a module is a design unit resolution issue, NOT a compilation scope error.; Legal packages, interfaces, or compilation directives MUST NOT be mechanically wrapped into a module just because they are outside a module.
cards.title: Module instances must be located in a legal scope within a design unit
verification: Run xvlog to check that compilation scope diagnostics disappear, then use xelab to expand the target top level and confirm the instance is in the expected hierarchy.

applies_when: xvlog 2026.1 reports that an explicit type must be specified at a declaration where a range is directly followed by an identifier.
guidance: First examine the complete declaration and the previous statement before the diagnostic location to confirm whether it is a missing type or a cascading result of parser recovery.
If the range and name are correct, select logic, wire, reg, or another real type based on the driving method and language mode.
hard_negatives: logic [K:0] already has an explicit type; if K is not evaluable at elaboration, route to the constant rule.
When a semicolon is missing in the previous line, hard-adding a type to the current identifier may create a second error.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN the declaration already has a legal type but the range expression is not constant, or the true root cause is a missing semicolon in the previous statement causing parser misalignment.

applies_when: It is confirmed that the declaration is missing a data type, and the object's port direction, driving method, range, and usage can be determined from the current candidate and specification.
guidance: Use declarations that can be carried by nets for continuous assignments or module output connections; use variable types allowed by the current language for procedural block assignments.
Retain confirmed packed/unpacked dimensions, signedness, and interface width; DO NOT guess new ranges based on diagnostic text.
After adding the type, check if an object with the same name already has a port or local declaration to avoid turning a missing type into a duplicate declaration.
hard_negatives: Uniformly changing to logic DOES NOT automatically resolve multi-driver issues or all net/variable distinctions in Verilog mode.
Adding a type when a preceding semicolon is missing may only change the location of the parse error.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN the error comes from a non-evaluable range, ANSI port duplicate declaration, previous statement syntax error, or the object usage is still unclear.

applies_when: In the same xvlog run, an unexplainable source byte or character is reported first, followed by a syntax error at a nearby location.
guidance: Preserve the diagnostic order of the same group, first locate and clean up evidenced abnormal bytes or rewrite that location with explicit encoding, then re-run parsing.
Only syntax errors that persist after re-running should be handed to local syntax repair; DO NOT simultaneously rewrite encoding and RTL structure on a large scale.
hard_negatives: Legal UTF-8 comments are NOT abnormal bytes; deleting all non-ASCII text will cause meaningless changes.
Pure missing semicolons or keyword context errors should directly use the local syntax card; encoding repair is NOT needed.
not_applicable_when: DO NOT USE WHEN the file is valid UTF-8 and has only independent syntax errors, or non-ASCII content appears only in comments and strings acceptable to the tool.

f24.projection_text:
[Knowledge Card repair-replication-concatenation-syntax@1.1.0-en.candidate.1 | compact]
Title: Use a replication expression as one item of an outer concatenation
Boundary: stages=lint; error_codes=VRFC 10-4982; tools=xvlog, xelab; versions=2026.1
Use when: 1. The parser reports an error near the comma after a replication expression, and the replicated value must be combined with a slice or another item to form a wider concatenation.
DO NOT USE when: 1. DO NOT USE WHEN the expression is only an independent replication item {N{expr}}, or when the first syntax error comes from a preceding statement, parenthesis, semicolon, or unmatched begin/end.
Method: 1. Write an independent replication expression as {N{expr}}; by itself it means N copies of expr.; 2. When the replicated value must be concatenated with a slice, add an outer pair of braces: {{N{expr}}, slice}.; 3. Compute the width of every item and confirm that their sum equals the destination width.
Verify: 1. Re-run xvlog/xelab to confirm the syntax diagnostic disappears, then test positive and negative sign bits plus boundary bits to verify extension direction and total width.
FORBIDDEN / hard negatives: 1. DO NOT delete the comma or slice and thereby degrade the required concatenation into a standalone replication.; 2. DO NOT replace arithmetic-right-shift sign extension with zero fill or change the destination port width merely to remove the syntax diagnostic.
Conflict groups: replication-item-versus-outer-concatenation, syntax-fix-versus-shift-semantics
